channel.title: NewsCenter — All newsletter news — 2026-11-11
channel.description: Every news received through Laurent's newsletters over the last 24 hours. 106 news received.

item.title: Anthropic unveils its Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 models
item.description: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, touting them as 30% faster and 20% cheaper than the 5.1 generation. The models underwent new safety and alignment testing.

item.title: The timeline of the espionage suspicions surrounding Jensen Huang
item.description: The article traces the timeline of the alleged espionage case involving Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s CEO.

item.title: Google unveils two new TPU chips and increases pressure on Nvidia
item.description: Google introduced two new versions of its eighth-generation TPUs, which are used to train and run Gemini. They are expected to ship in 2027, while TPU sales could exceed $135 billion in 2028.

item.title: OpenAI creates a kill switch for its research models
item.description: OpenAI developed Control Room, a system capable of cutting off a research AI model’s access to its outputs. It tracks training, evaluations and data processing, but a cached authorization can delay shutdown by 35 seconds.

item.title: METR estimates that Anthropic’s measured progress has accelerated 1.9-fold
item.description: METR estimates that Anthropic’s benchmark-measured progress has been about 1.9 times faster since October 2025. The organization considers it likely that artificial intelligence is behind most of this acceleration.

item.title: Reddit turns user conversations into AI-generated product reviews
item.description: Reddit is turning its users’ conversations into artificial intelligence-generated product reviews.

item.title: Adobe adds AI agents to Photoshop, Premiere and Firefly
item.description: Adobe is bringing artificial intelligence agents and new creative tools to Photoshop, Premiere and Firefly.

item.title: Claude Code accidentally exposes secrets on GitHub
item.description: Claude Code accidentally exposed secret information on GitHub.

item.title: How Product Hunt nearly disappeared
item.description: The article examines how Product Hunt almost disappeared.

item.title: Anthropic maintains its IPO plans despite turbulence
item.description: Anthropic plans to begin trading its shares by the end of next week. Investors were targeting a valuation of about $1.5 trillion, but some are now seeking a lower figure, while the company could still delay the offering.

item.title: Meta can still rely on advertising if its AI bet fails
item.description: Even if Meta’s bet on artificial intelligence fails, the company still has its advertising business as a fallback.

item.title: Jensen Huang scandal unlikely to derail the AI market
item.description: Despite Nvidia’s 4.3% decline, the scandal is not expected to trigger a collapse in the artificial intelligence market. Analysts explain why the sector could continue to grow.

item.title: ChatGPT exceeds 81% of traffic to leading AI chatbots
item.description: ChatGPT now accounts for more than 81% of traffic to the six leading AI chatbots, according to a Graphite study. Its growth resumed after a period of stagnation, pulling ahead of Claude and Gemini.

item.title: Religious investor downplays importance of Anthropic IPO
item.description: A faith-based investor shares his view on Anthropic’s IPO and says the company is not the savior of the universe.

item.title: OpenAI tests its agents on real-world biology experiments
item.description: With biotech company Ligo, OpenAI is launching BioBasicsBench, a test of 100 tasks based on raw experimental data. The agents must interpret DNA gels, culture plates, microscope images and flow cytometry, among other things.

item.title: Instagram expands detection of teens lying about their age
item.description: Meta is rolling out AI detection worldwide on Instagram to identify teens who entered a false adult birth date. These accounts are automatically switched to Teen Accounts, with restrictions on contacts, content and time spent.

item.title: OpenAI makes ChatGPT Enterprise available in AWS Marketplace
item.description: AWS customers can now purchase ChatGPT Enterprise through cloud billing and their existing spending commitments.

item.title: SpaceX seeks tax relief for its $24 billion energy project
item.description: SpaceX is seeking tax relief for the initial phases of a gas-fired power plant and a supercomputer project valued at around $24 billion at Starbase, Texas.

item.title: A Silicon Valley therapist analyzes Jensen Huang’s infidelity
item.description: Phil Boissierie, a Silicon Valley couples therapist, shares advice for high-profile clients concerned about their own infidelities. According to him, Jensen Huang’s affair offers lessons for high-profile couples.

item.title: An affair allegedly facilitated the shipment of $7.5 billion in chips to China
item.description: According to The Information, Jensen Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang may have helped move at least $7.5 billion worth of restricted Nvidia chips to Chinese companies. Around 240,000 H- and A-series chips were allegedly shipped, some to Alibaba and Tencent.

item.title: Ring unveils a flying camera and a surveillance robot
item.description: Ring unveiled the Drone Cam, a $250 flying camera, and the Rover Cam, a ground robot, which will go on sale starting January 27, 2027. The Drone Cam includes 2K and 1080p cameras and uses the AI Pilot cloud system to navigate the home.

item.title: Meta’s smallest AI model competes with Claude Haiku
item.description: Meta launched Muse Ember, its smallest and cheapest AI model, which reportedly matches Claude Haiku 5.5 on some intelligence scores. It is designed for repetitive agent tasks and can process up to one million multimodal tokens, but its weights remain private.

item.title: Google DeepMind mathematically verifies Signal’s encryption
item.description: Google DeepMind says its AI agents mathematically proved the validity of the Signal protocol’s code. They generated more than six million lines of Lean in four weeks and detected two old bugs that had been deliberately reintroduced.

item.title: Anthropic targets a $1.02 trillion valuation
item.description: The article outlines Anthropic’s valuation ambitions, with the company reportedly seeking to reach $1.02 trillion.

item.title: Apple launches $50 intelligence usage plans
item.description: Apple is launching $50 intelligence usage plans for certain AI features.

item.title: Uber launches its own parking reservation service
item.description: Uber is preparing to launch a service that lets users reserve parking spaces.

item.title: U.S. sues Lyft over discrimination against passengers with disabilities
item.description: The United States is accusing Lyft of discriminating against passengers with disabilities.

item.title: Medium integrates AI writing assistance with its new TK app
item.description: Medium is launching the TK app, which integrates AI assistance directly into the writing process.

item.title: Waze rolls out cyclist alerts powered by Garmin data
item.description: Waze is rolling out cyclist alerts based on real-time location data provided by Garmin trackers.

item.title: Moonshot AI reportedly rented Nvidia’s top chips in China
item.description: Bloomberg reports that Moonshot AI rented high-end Nvidia chips in China.

item.title: France accuses Iran of cyberattacks on supermarket refrigerators
item.description: France accuses Iran of carrying out cyberattacks against supermarket refrigerators and is considering sanctions.

item.title: North Korea reportedly uses Elon Musk memecoins to launder cryptocurrency
item.description: North Korea is reportedly using memecoins linked to Elon Musk to launder cryptocurrency stolen in the Binance hack.

item.title: Higgsfield unveils Miracle, a real-time video editing tool
item.description: Higgsfield unveiled Miracle, a pre-launch tool that lets users modify an existing video by describing changes while it plays. Announced edits include moving objects, changing colors and adjusting speed, without regenerating the scene.

item.title: Atmee v2 creates a talking avatar in real time from an image
item.description: Atmanity launched Atmee v2, a real-time avatar model that turns an image and a short voice clip into an avatar users can talk to. The company claims it is up to 50 times faster and 10 to 100 times cheaper than leading video models, but these figures have not been independently verified.

item.title: Thinking Machines launches Inkling 2 Small, an open-weight vision model
item.description: Thinking Machines launched Inkling 2 Small, a second-generation model for coding, research and extended office work, with vision as its primary capability. The model correctly identified three wines from a photo in 19 out of 20 trials, and its full weights are expected to be released under the Apache 2.0 license the following week.

item.title: Apple pushes an autonomous Siri agent without a confirmed timeline
item.description: According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, Apple is working on an autonomous Siri agent, but the company has not yet provided a timeline.

item.title: Perplexity launches background agents for its Max subscribers
item.description: Perplexity launched Teammates, background agents that handle ongoing projects and notify users when a decision is needed. The feature is available to Max subscribers on the web and iOS.

item.title: Design Arena compares generative image models
item.description: Design Arena ranks generative image models in head-to-head matchups. The service lets users choose a generator to try before subscribing to a paid plan.

item.title: Overuse of AI can create a speed trap in the workplace
item.description: AI can produce work faster than teams can understand it, potentially increasing confusion. The text recommends continuing to learn, adding one’s own perspective and asking authors to defend AI-assisted results.

item.title: Outlook.com rejects legitimate emails after authentication tightening
item.description: Microsoft’s consumer email services are rejecting legitimate messages following changes to sender authentication enforcement. SPF and DMARC validation failures have been reported, including for seemingly compliant domains.

item.title: Rising memory prices make refurbished hardware more attractive
item.description: Surging memory prices are increasing interest in refurbished PCs and enterprise equipment. Suppliers are seeing growing demand for extending device lifespans, buybacks and warrantied equipment.

item.title: Companies prepare for the mass arrival of personal AI agents
item.description: Companies are preparing for increased traffic generated by personal AI agents such as Meta’s Muse and Instinct, viewed both as commercial channels and governance challenges. Shopify, Hilton and Rocket are among those adapting their platforms and APIs.

item.title: AI and business transformation redefine the CIO’s role
item.description: The CIO’s role is shifting from managing technology delivery to redesigning business processes and demonstrating measurable results. Technology leaders must now address productivity, organizational change and accountability for decisions made with AI.

item.title: China could face greater exposure to the risks of a cyber-apocalypse
item.description: AI-driven vulnerability discovery is accelerating the race between identifying and fixing flaws. China’s state-led cybersecurity strategy and restrictions on vulnerability disclosure could put its systems at a disadvantage.

item.title: Virtual machines remain central to cloud-native infrastructure
item.description: A Linux Foundation study of 492 professionals found that virtual machines account for an average of 53% of production applications. Most respondents expect their VM footprint to remain relatively stable despite growing Kubernetes adoption.

item.title: Google Cloud offers self-managed VMware Cloud Foundation on bare-metal servers
item.description: Google Cloud has made a self-managed VMware Cloud Foundation solution generally available on dedicated bare-metal hardware in 22 regions. Customers have root access to ESXi, vCenter and NSX and manage upgrades and patches themselves.

item.title: Red Hat launches OpenShift 5 with more automated cloud management
item.description: Red Hat announced the general availability of OpenShift 5, which introduces AI-assisted troubleshooting, anomaly detection and supervised remediation. The release also expands unified support for containers, virtual machines and AI workloads.

item.title: Broadcom contributes its open-source VM API project to the CNCF
item.description: Broadcom’s VM API project was accepted into the CNCF Sandbox to provide a vendor-independent way to manage virtual machines through Kubernetes APIs. Broadcom also announced its participation in a workload compliance initiative.

item.title: Cisco builds an enterprise AI platform to improve GPU utilization
item.description: Cisco IT developed a multi-tenant AI infrastructure platform combining shared networking, NVIDIA and AMD GPUs, rack-level cooling, and integrated security. Cisco says it tripled average GPU utilization, from 15% to about 50%, and increased its GPU fleet sixfold.

item.title: AI coding agents can increase developer burnout
item.description: Managing AI coding agents can increase developer fatigue because of constant context switching, decision fatigue, and pressure to keep agents active. These mechanisms can lead developers to delegate more and more decisions to AI without fully understanding the results.

item.title: AI spending is rising without causing a “SaaSpocalypse”
item.description: Data indicates that increased AI spending is not cannibalizing traditional software budgets. Companies heavily invested in AI have also increased their software spending.

item.title: Google simplifies confirmation of classification labels in Workspace
item.description: Google is making it easier to verify classification labels automatically applied to Google Drive, Docs, Sheets, and Slides files. New buttons let users accept or modify them.

item.title: Startup Nominal triples its valuation to $3 billion in eight months
item.description: Nominal raised $240 million in a Series C round at a valuation of $3 billion. Its valuation was $1 billion in March.

item.title: Difference will become a scarce resource in the AI era
item.description: When AI produces most content, value will lie in the things it does not do. A cheap variation will not be equivalent to a sufficiently distinctive difference that attracts attention and justifies payment.

item.title: An mRNA therapy helps mice repair their hearts
item.description: Researchers developed an mRNA therapy that reactivates heart muscle cells so they divide and repair damage. The treatment strengthened mice’s heartbeats after a heart attack, but trials in larger animal models are needed before any human testing.

item.title: Storybook 11 beta adds tools for AI agents
item.description: Storybook provides an isolated environment for developing and testing an application’s component variants. The Storybook 11 beta introduces official skills and headless CLI tools that let agents iterate autonomously, in a smaller package with faster context handoffs.

item.title: chrome-capture records Chrome tabs in MP4 at up to 2160p
item.description: With Chrome 153 and later versions, chrome-capture records tabs at 60 to 120 frames per second, up to 2160p, directly in AVI .mp4 format. The tool includes tab audio and encodes AV1 while recording.

item.title: Software will eventually be created instantly on demand
item.description: Software will gradually evolve until it no longer really means anything, since anything digital will be able to be created instantly at will.

item.title: Writing serves to externalize and structure thought
item.description: Language allows part of thought to be externalized, and writing externalizes an even larger portion of it.

item.title: Investigations target Nvidia for potentially misleading investors
item.description: Investigations are underway to determine whether Nvidia misled its investors.

item.title: Wing will build a delivery drone factory in Texas
item.description: Wing, an Alphabet subsidiary, plans to build a 15,000-square-foot factory in Fort Worth. It will be able to produce tens of thousands of aircraft per year.

item.title: Who could replace Jensen Huang at Nvidia?
item.description: Replacing Jensen Huang would be particularly complex because he runs Nvidia day to day and embodies both the company and the AI industry. Geoff Weiss analyzes the candidates who could succeed him.

item.title: Wall Street strategists bet on an AI rebound again
item.description: After the sell-off that hit the AI market following the midterm elections, investors are buying the dip. Strategists now expect gains by the end of the year.

item.title: Morgan Stanley proposes a three-part strategy for investing in AI
item.description: Morgan Stanley considers the market’s reaction to the Democratic wave in the midterm elections excessive. The bank recommends investing in hyperscalers, data-center suppliers and companies adopting AI.

item.title: Goldman Sachs’ new partners describe how they celebrated their promotions
item.description: Goldman Sachs promoted 109 people to its partnership. Six new partners describe how they learned the news and celebrated their promotions.

item.title: TikTok Shop strengthens the influence of its Chinese executives
item.description: A leaked organizational chart reveals that China-based executives have increased their power over TikTok Shop. ByteDance sold much of its stake in the U.S. version while retaining tight control of Shop.

item.title: California billionaires avoid a new tax
item.description: California voters rejected Proposition 40, which would have imposed a one-time 5% tax on fortunes exceeding $1 billion. Silicon Valley executives largely funded the opposition campaign.

item.title: An $8 surcharge reveals the scale of hidden fees in the U.S.
item.description: A journalist thought she would pay $20 for a haircut before discovering an $8 surcharge. The experience led her to investigate the hidden-fee epidemic, estimated at $90 billion.

item.title: Andrew Huberman joins the board of Hims&Hers
item.description: Stanford neuroscientist and podcaster Andrew Huberman is joining the board of Hims&Hers. He will advise the company directly on scientific matters and marketing, without changing the topics of his podcast.

item.title: Disney+ prepares creator content and a free tier
item.description: Disney’s technology executives presented Disney+’s priorities for the coming year. They include expanding into creator content and launching a free offering.

item.title: Skydance executives address employees after strong results
item.description: Skydance’s CEOs spoke to employees after the company beat forecasts in its first earnings report.

item.title: Four tech CEOs explain how they handled relationship scandals
item.description: The article examines how four technology executives handled scandals involving their personal relationships.

item.title: Cohere alumni launch law firm after leaving the company
item.description: Employees left Cohere to pursue careers in law. They say their new firm can avoid the fate experienced by Weil.

item.title: Paramount+ and HBO Max to prepare a bundled offering
item.description: A bundle combining Paramount+ and HBO Max is in the works. Skydance outlined the timeline for bringing its streaming services together.

item.title: James Gunn and Peter Safran leave DC Studios
item.description: James Gunn and Peter Safran will leave their positions at DC Studios.

item.title: Apple harvest expected to be particularly poor for U.S. orchards
item.description: Local apple orchards are facing an especially difficult year.

item.title: Legal startup generates $150 million without targeting major firms
item.description: A legal startup says it generates $150 million in revenue without seeking to compete directly with major law firms.

item.title: Meituan releases LongCat-2.5, a very low-cost open-source coding model
item.description: Meituan is releasing the weights of LongCat-2.5 under the MIT license, a multimodal model that can analyze screenshots and videos before coding in multiple steps. Its API access is priced at $0.30 per million input tokens, compared with $5 for Claude Opus 5.

item.title: Bytedance unveils Seedream 5.5 for editing an image up to 100 times
item.description: Seedream 5.5 supports up to 100 successive edits while preserving unchanged areas and colors. The model also natively generates RGBA images and is gradually rolling out across several Bytedance services.

item.title: Meta launches Muse Ember, nearly as capable as its larger model
item.description: Meta is launching Muse Ember, a small model designed for agents’ repetitive tasks, such as tool calling, routing and data extraction. It achieves nearly the same score as Muse Spark 1.3 at 17 times lower cost per task.

item.title: HOPE halves a large model without retraining
item.description: Amazon researchers propose HOPE, a method that removes the least useful experts while accounting for their interactions. It removes 50% of experts and notably improves agentic coding performance compared with the best competing method.

item.title: Law firms split between time savings and resistance to agents
item.description: Legal industry leaders describe the gains enabled by agents, including bringing outsourced tasks back in-house. Many lawyers, however, remain limited to document summaries because of fatigue or fear of losing billable time.

item.title: Paramount chief sees AI as a major transformation for filmmaking
item.description: David Ellison calls AI “the greatest creative lever in modern history” and compares it with the arrival of computer-generated imagery in the 1990s. No concrete project has been announced, however.

item.title: Researchers propose “cognitive symbiotes” rather than autonomous agents
item.description: A paper proposes persistent AI companions that remember context, spot forgotten details, and intervene at the right moment. The approach aims to strengthen human reasoning but remains conceptual and raises risks involving dependence, privacy, and equity.

item.title: Muir improves model efficiency on long texts
item.description: Muir is a linear-attention architecture that focuses its resources on the most important information in internal memory. On small models, it retrieves information from long documents more effectively and speeds up training by 2.7 times at 32K context.

item.title: DeepX announces a chip capable of running 100 billion parameters under 5 watts
item.description: Korean manufacturer DeepX claims it can run models with up to 100 billion parameters using less than 5 watts. The second-generation chip is ready for manufacturing, but the reported gains remain the manufacturer’s projections.

item.title: Coalition opposes Google data center near London
item.description: In Thurrock, the Buglife association, NGO Foxglove, and a motorcycle club delivered a petition with nearly 55,000 signatures to Google. They denounce the project’s effects on a rare plant and bumblebee, pollution, and the loss of a former motorcycle track.

item.title: Tencent wants to remove dangerous knowledge from training data
item.description: Tencent’s chief AI scientist believes AI will soon be able to design biological weapons, but says closing models is not a solution. For its future open model Hy4, Tencent plans to remove dangerous knowledge directly from the training data.

item.title: US companies without employees are growing with AI
item.description: In sectors exposed to AI, new businesses with no plans to hire increased by 26.8% between early 2024 and early 2026. New businesses planning to recruit fell by 6.4%, but a causal link to AI has not yet been established.

item.title: Claude reveals more than 100 vulnerabilities in UK government projects
item.description: Using Claude Opus and Sonnet, a researcher found vulnerabilities in roughly two-thirds of 349 public projects belonging to 33 UK organizations. One vulnerability provided read and write access to SharePoint and OneDrive spaces containing HR files.

item.title: Trump downplays AI risks on 60 Minutes
item.description: Donald Trump considers the risk posed by AI “far less real” than industry leaders say and claims it is controlled by the Justice Department. He also recounted an unverifiable anecdote about an AI company executive threatened with prison.

item.title: Nothing will launch its first AI device in December
item.description: Nothing will launch its first AI-native productivity device in December, without a new screen. Carl Pei mentions novel contextual features, with details to be revealed soon.

item.title: Aina’s AI ring turns the thumb into an approval button
item.description: Aina’s $399 ring offers contextual actions approved with a thumb movement, such as booking a ride, managing meetings, or answering calls. IT professionals should specifically verify compatibility, permissions, and audit trails.

item.title: Nvidia strengthens AI chip tracking in Southeast Asia
item.description: Nvidia now requires its Southeast Asian cloud partners to enroll in Fleet Intelligence to strengthen GPU tracking, amid allegations of chip smuggling to China. The measure could affect partner status, GPU availability, and compliance with export rules.

item.title: Cursor can create and deploy web applications from prompts
item.description: Cursor’s Build Live Apps feature generates, secures, and deploys complete applications with a database, authentication, and hosting. It aims to reduce setup time for internal tools, but its security and pricing limitations should be examined.

item.title: Google’s AI video model cuts prices by 30%
item.description: Google’s Omni 1.2 Flash cuts the cost of AI video generation by 30% and produces clips of up to 15 seconds. It can generate 720p videos at $0.07 per second, with multi-turn editing and improved consistency.

item.title: AI becomes widespread as threats and pressures increase
item.description: AI is being deployed everywhere and creating new security and infrastructure problems. Generative advances, attacks, and cost pressures are reshaping corporate priorities.

item.title: Five Canva alternatives for businesses in 2027
item.description: Adobe Express, Visme, VistaCreate, Figma, and Piktochart each address specific professional needs, from branding to data visualization. The article recommends testing these solutions for two weeks before switching tools.

item.title: AI data center boom prompts political backlash in the United States
item.description: Voters have opposed the growth of AI-dedicated data centers, and new restrictions could slow construction, raise costs, and alter capacity distribution. The affected regions, regulations, and business risks remain worth monitoring.

item.title: Disney and Adobe to create AI image models trained on the Disney universe
item.description: Disney is developing its own AI image models based on its characters, settings and styles. The multi-year partnership with Adobe is expected to produce generators for parks, cruises, production and marketing, among other uses.

item.title: Fireworks AI confirms billing and model data breach
item.description: Attackers accessed customer billing data, excluding card numbers, as well as model weights and incomplete datasets for some customers. Fireworks links the incident to a group that resells access to stolen AI accounts.

item.title: Cisco integrates Anthropic’s Claude Mythos into its AI defense offering
item.description: Cisco plans to add Claude Mythos to AI Defense so some companies can run adaptive red-team tests on their own AI applications.

item.title: Liquid Energy unveils NanoDC, a prefabricated solar AI data center
item.description: The Y Combinator startup claims that NanoDC, a factory-built solar data center for AI, can be deployed in four weeks. These figures are company-reported.

item.title: Adobe study says AI is accelerating growth for many creators
item.description: According to Adobe’s survey, 78% of creative AI users believe these tools have accelerated the growth of their business or audience. The study also says that 68% at least sometimes accept results that do not match their vision.

item.title: Why AI pilots still struggle to reach enterprise scale
item.description: The article examines why successful AI pilot projects still have difficulty being deployed at scale in enterprises.

item.title: The Value Stack helps prioritize customer benefits
item.description: Customers do not place equal importance on every benefit: some determine their choice, others reinforce it, while “table stakes” are simply expected. Strategyzer’s Value Stack organizes these benefits into three categories to help build a more differentiated value proposition.
